chapters.title: 1. Why We Need a Verifier: Search vs Check
chapters.question: Could you explain what a verifier is?
chapters.insight: Searching from scratch explores 2^n possibilities, whereas a verifier V(x, w) checks one proposed certificate w in O(n^k) time.
chapters.narration: Branching from your question: let us unpack exactly what a verifier is and how it works. Rather than searching an exponential tree of possibilities from scratch, a verifier V(x, w) is a fast deterministic algorithm that checks whether a proposed witness w solves problem instance x.

chapters.title: 2. Inside the Verifier Gate V(x, w)
chapters.question: How does V(x, w) process the instance x and witness w step by step?
chapters.insight: Instance x and Witness w feed together into V(x, w), which runs polynomial local checks in sequence before lighting the YES beacon.
chapters.narration: Now watch the verifier gate V(x, w) operate in live 3Blue1Brown geometry. chapters.title: 3. The Two Laws of an NP Verifier
chapters.question: What two mathematical rules must V(x, w) obey to define Class NP?
chapters.insight: To qualify as an NP verifier, the witness w must have polynomial length |w| <= |x|^k AND the checker V(x, w) must halt in polynomial time O(|x|^k).
chapters.narration: Why can we not hide an exponential list inside the witness? Two strict polynomial rules keep verification honest. First, the certificate w must be polynomially short so it can even be read; second, V(x, w) must verify all constraints in deterministic O(n^k) time, turning Sudoku, TSP, and SAT into fast verification problems.

continuity.bridge: Why can we not hide an exponential list inside the witness? Two strict polynomial rules keep verification honest.

cues.text: Why can we not hide an exponential list inside the witness?
Two strict polynomial rules keep verification honest.

First, the certificate w must be polynomially short so it can even be read; second, V(x, w) must verify all constraints in deterministic O(n^k) time, turning Sudoku, TSP, and SAT into fast verification problems.

roles.law-short: 1. Short Witness (|w| <= |x|^k): The certificate w cannot be exponentially long; its bit-length is bounded by a polynomial in |x|.
roles.law-fast: 2. Fast Check (O(|x|^k) steps): Given x and w, the deterministic machine V(x, w) finishes checking in polynomial time.
roles.law-sound: 3. Soundness & Completeness: x is a YES instance if and only if there EXISTS at least one witness w where V(x, w) = YES.

First, the certificate w must be polynomially short so it can even be read; second, V(x, w) must verify all constraints in deterministic O(n^k) time, turning Sudoku, TSP, and SAT into fast verification problems.
